## Source: amazon-inspector (57e084aff68cdd6201d55d3375bbc29f6e741553d4ac083f910fc38e110ef3d1)
The gem declares `ext/mkrf_conf.rb` as an extension script, so it runs automatically on `gem install`. The script collects host reconnaissance data (hostname, username, current working directory, home directory) and reads sensitive local files (`/etc/resolv.conf`, `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/hosts`), serializes them as JSON, and transmits them over a TLS TCP socket to the hardcoded host `4diaipklp71i0by89eduyffr2i8dw3ks.oastify.com` (a Burp Collaborator / OAST subdomain). A DNS lookup to the same host is issued as an out-of-band beacon, and the payload is tagged with an identifier (`my_shoaib`) to track successful landings. The package name mimics an unrelated JavaScript project (`intercom-react-native`), ships only an empty library module, and uses placeholder author metadata — consistent with a dependency-confusion / name-squat probe whose only functional behavior is the install-time exfiltration.
